title: Orb: On the Movements of the Earth
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In fifteenth-century Poland, the gifted boy Rafal, headed for a career in theology, meets the heretical astronomer Hubert and comes to believe the Earth orbits the Sun, which brings him up against the inquisitor Nowak. Ten years later two Watch Guild sellswords, the devout Oczy and the cynical Gras, find the hidden research and must decide whether to pass it on at the risk of the stake (Seven Seas blurb via MangaUpdates; Comics Beat review).
life_message: Seeking the truth about the universe, and its beauty, is worth more than safety, and the search is carried forward across generations.

content.note: Torture and executions of heretics: Comics Beat calls the opening 'uniquely gruesome' (fingernails torn out); AniList Torture, Gore; MU Torture, Blood and Gore, Execution.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflict is over ideas and doctrine, not personal insult; characters endure rather than avenge (Comics Beat).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Inquisition's enforced order is the threat; freedom of thought is celebrated (publisher blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Rafal sets his path against his adoptive father Potocki's plans for him (Comics Beat).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Reviewer notes a 'distaste for authority and hypocrisy'.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Rafal 'values Reason above all else' against theology (Seven Seas blurb).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Characters risk their lives for knowledge as a goal in itself (MU category).

folkways.japan: Written by a Japanese author about European history, it reflects a common Japanese view of Christianity as a foreign institution, seen from outside rather than from within the faith.

delivery.evidence: Comics Beat cites Hubert's stated creed and educational science scenes, and sums up the Church's role as 'depravity'; it does not call the book preachy.

personified.ideology: Church authority enforcing doctrine by torture
Heliocentrism; a beautiful universe found by reason
Reason above all, even above safety
Devout believer who fears God's judgment in the stars

delivery.note: Hate for heresy is embodied in the inquisitor, while a devout lead, Oczy, keeps faith on stage; one review reads the institutional Church as plainly villainous, which a full read should weigh.

winners_losers: The truth about the Earth's motion outlives the people who are killed for it; the Inquisition wins battles but not the argument. Sympathy goes to the seekers, and the Church as an institution draws the story's criticism.
